narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 90.8% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because the law school sets a high bar for admission and wants students likely to succeed, this high risk of failure led to your application being rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors, ranked by importance. Your first-year and third-year class rankings had the strongest influence, both pushing the prediction strongly toward failure. Being in the bottom decile for grades in both Year 1 and Year 3, compared to an average around the 6th decile among accepted students, signaled consistent academic struggle in law school. Your LSAT score was the third most important factor and also pulled the prediction toward failure. At 27, it sits well below the average of 37 among those who were admitted.

Other details such as your undergraduate GPA of 3.20, middle family income, full-time status, gender, and race played much smaller roles and were not major drivers of the outcome.

To improve your chances, focus on strengthening your academic performance and consider retaking the LSAT to raise your score. Building a stronger record in these key areas will help future applications demonstrate a clearer path to passing the bar. (198 words)
